title: Account Director, Federal Partnerships (Defense)
description:
About the team

OpenAI’s mission is to build safe artificial general intelligence (AGI) which benefits all of humanity. This long-term undertaking brings the world’s best scientists, engineers, and business professionals into one lab together to accomplish this.

In pursuit of this mission, our Go To Market (GTM) team is responsible for helping customers learn how to leverage and deploy our highly capable AI products across their organization. The team comprises Sales, Solutions, Support, Marketing, and Partnership professionals who collaborate to create valuable solutions that will help bring AI to as many users as possible.

About the role

Our Federal Partnerships team brings advanced AI to the defense industrial base. You’ll own a portfolio of emerging defense technology accounts and lead their account and deal strategy. You’ll also work with the broader partnerships team to grow larger strategic relationships.

You’ll independently lead customer meetings and manage your assigned emerging defense technology portfolio, working with technical teams to turn customer needs into deployed capabilities. This is a demanding, hands-on role that requires initiative, persistence, and a strong sense of responsibility for getting useful AI capabilities into customers’ hands.

This role is based in Washington, DC, with up to 25% travel. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you'll:

- Lead account strategy and commercial execution for your emerging defense technology portfolio, from discovery and negotiation through close and expansion.

- Support the broader partnerships team on larger strategic relationships across the defense industrial base.

- Work with solutions and engineering teams to move customers from AI evaluation to deployment and sustained adoption.

- Maintain accurate pipeline, consumption forecasts, and clear next steps.

- Build trusted executive and technical relationships, connecting AI capabilities to business and mission outcomes.

- Anticipate customer needs and bring customer and market insights into product and partnership decisions.

- Coordinate across OpenAI to advance deals, remove blockers, and deliver on customer commitments.

We're seeking someone with:

- 8+ years of combined relevant experience across government, military service, defense technology, or PaaS/SaaS businesses, including at least 2 years in private-sector, customer-facing roles.

- Proven private-sector results, with clear examples of business or customer outcomes you personally drove.

- Strong business acumen and strategic judgment, including the ability to assess opportunities, navigate stakeholders, and turn insight into action.

- The ability to take initiative, set priorities, and deliver results amid the ambiguity and pace of defense technology.

- Polished, clear communication and experience working directly with senior executives in government or the private sector.

- Hands-on experience applying AI tools to practical problems, with the ability to explain the approach, results, and limitations. Strong understanding of APIs and workflow integration, with the ability to engage engineering teams credibly.

- Military service and/or defense technology experience are valued.

- Initiative, urgency, and coachability, with a record of acting on feedback and following through.

You might thrive in this role if you: 

- Are customer-centric. You understand customers’ priorities and take ownership of helping them deploy useful capabilities quickly.

- Are deeply curious about AI. You regularly test new capabilities, explore their limits, and identify practical uses for customers.

- Bring a strong work ethic. You take initiative, prepare thoroughly, and follow through. You move quickly through ambiguity without sacrificing judgment or trust.

- Look ahead. You anticipate what customers will need next and help them identify new opportunities.

The Accountant II reports to the Accounting Manager and owns key parts of Clearwave’s monthly close, from journal entries and accruals to balance sheet reconciliations, cash forecasting and intercompany accounting. • Analyze actual-to-budget variances and explain key drivers

• Cash Management

•

• Manage cash balances and prepare the weekly cash forecast

• Prepare the weekly Cash Position report vs. budget and forecast

• Intercompany

•

• Record the monthly intercompany journal entry and markup fee

• Issue intercompany invoices and reconcile intercompany balances

• Document accounting procedures and maintain the month-end close checklist

•

• Oversee the accounts payable process, including vendor setup, invoice approval and payment runs

• Monitor payables aging and due dates

• Own the employee expense and corporate card process, including policy compliance and staff training

• Review expenses for trends and accuracy

• Manage recurring expenses and allowances

• Special ad hoc responsibilities and projects.

Requirements

• Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance and 3-5 years of progressive general ledger accounting experience; CPA or CPA-track preferred.

• Strong working knowledge of U.S. GAAP, accrual accounting and month-end close, including account reconciliations, accruals, prepaids and fixed assets.

• Advanced Excel skills and the ability to turn data into clear financial analysis.

• Experience using, or a strong interest in using, AI tools such as Claude to streamline accounting workflows, reconciliations, analysis and reporting.

• SaaS or software industry experience a plus; familiarity with ASC 606 preferred.

• Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet close deadlines.

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Mercor’s evals product helps frontier labs and enterprises understand how their models perform on real work. title: Senior Mechanical Engineer, Thermal-Fluid Systems
description:
About Skyven
At Skyven Technologies , we are replacing industrial boilers with electric heat pumps that make process steam at a lower cost than burning fuel. Under the hood, our Arcturus heat pump is an open-cycle mechanical vapor recompression (MVR) system: we flash hot water to low-pressure steam, then compress that steam with multi-stage centrifugal machinery up to the pressure the plant needs. We give our customers two options to deploy the heat pump: (A) a traditional CAPEX purchase, and (B) an innovative Energy-as-a-Service (EaaS) model with zero CAPEX and savings from day one. Either way, customers save money and reduce emissions while minimizing risk.
We are past the lab: our first commercial systems are in execution at industrial customer sites, and we keep pushing the technology at our Demo Center. This is a role for someone who wants to do serious engineering in a startup environment: move quickly, think deeply, work with strong people, and help turn ambitious concepts into equipment that works in the field.
Why This Role

• You will be the lead mechanical engineer on the first commercial units of a new class of multi-megawatt industrial machine, not the next copy of a proven design.

• Your designs get built and run in operating plants, and your decisions will carry into every unit that follows.

• You get both halves of engineering: first-principles design on novel equipment, and the rigor of real industrial execution.

• Small team, real influence: you work directly with the CTO, and your judgment shapes the product.
About the Role
We are looking for a Senior Mechanical Engineer who exemplifies strong engineering judgment combined with strong practical mechanical engineering capability. We especially value engineers who have spent time close to real hardware in the field and know the difference between what looks good on paper and what really works.
You will own the mechanical side of our first commercial deployments, from P&ID through vendor selection, drawings, fabrication, and startup. Most of your time will go to project execution, with the rest on product development for future sites. You will bring deep practical mechanical judgment to the team’s system-level and conceptual thinking, turning ambitious concepts into designs that can actually be built, commissioned, operated, and maintained. This is an individual contributor role, but we are looking for someone with the maturity and breadth to grow into the technical lead for our mechanical systems.
This role is for someone who is energized by understanding how an entire system works, not just producing drawings or sourcing parts. You should be the kind of engineer who wants to understand the “why” behind requirements, spot weaknesses in a design, ask hard questions early, and improve a system’s performance, operability, reliability, and cost. One day that may mean digging into system architecture, operability, or failure modes. Another day it may mean reviewing a P&ID, building CAD, tightening a spec, challenging a vendor design, or catching issues in a drawing package before they become field problems.
What You’ll Work On
Arcturus is an industrial steam system, not an HVAC unit. The hardware and physics you will own include:

• Saturated water and steam systems from vacuum up to tens of bar: flash vessels, hot water recirculation, condensate return, venting, and draining

• Multi-megawatt, multi-stage centrifugal steam compression (larger systems exceed 10 MWe), plus the motors, VFDs, and controls around it

• Skidded and modular packages, pressure vessels, and the piping, supports, and thermal growth that tie them together

• Integration into operating plants: utility tie-ins, battery limits, outdoor installation, and freeze protection
